quantitative_evidence: FAI3 74.6%, FAI5 75.5%, FAI1 76.1% favourable; 137 records have at least one FAI item at 1–3
qualitative_evidence: Fairness prompt: 67 career/learning, 66 recognition and 64 communication requests; 73 no-concern replies

baseline_and_success_measures: Baseline FAI1/FAI3/FAI5; review criteria coverage, employee understanding and procedural consistency
interpretation_limit: 1–3 includes Sometimes; no universal unfairness or discrimination finding; mixed experiences retained

qualitative_evidence: 179 unique records request recognition/feedback; fairness–recognition pair support 57 answers / 53 records

baseline_and_success_measures: Baseline RES4/CAM5; track access to recognition and quality/usefulness of feedback
interpretation_limit: Topic includes performance feedback, not only awards; do not assume gifts resolve perceived fairness

baseline_and_success_measures: Baseline FAI4; establish operational backup/after-hours measures and review whether staff can use the arrangements
interpretation_limit: No validated burnout diagnosis or workload-volume measure; specific accounts require verification

quantitative_evidence: CRE5 79.8% favourable; 80/327 choose HR Communication as their one priority
qualitative_evidence: 134 records request voice/action and 194 communication/explanations; overlapping prompted topics

proposed_owner: Leadership and HR with relevant action owners
baseline_and_success_measures: Baseline CRE5; establish acknowledgement/closure times and ask whether employees saw useful change
interpretation_limit: Communication frequency alone is not proof of listening or problem resolution
